newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NatMut says expects equity stake in China.
newsitem.headline: NatMut says expects equity stake in China.

text.p: Australian life office National Mutual Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it expected to take an equity stake in the new China life insurance business of its French parent Axa-UAP.

National Mutual managing director Geoff Tomlinson, commenting on news that Axa-UAP will be awarded entry to China, said the two companies had agreed that the Australian-based subsidiary would serve as AXA-UAP'S Asian vehicle.
"I think the expectation of those agreements is that you (National Mutual) would have some equity participation," Tomlinson said.
One insurance analyst has suggested Axa-UAP shareholders would be reluctant to hand ownership of the potentially-lucrative China business to National Mutual.
Instead, the only role National Mutual was likely to play was as manager of the business through its Hong Kong-based subsidiary, National Mutual Asia, the analyst said.
National Mutual confirmed recently that Axa-UAP had been verbally advised by Chinese authorities it would be granted a licence to operate in Shanghai.
The licence would be in Axa-UAP's name only.
Australia's Foreign Investment Review Board (FIRB), which approved Axa's investment in National Mutual in 1995, has also raised the stakes.
The FIRB has said that a condition of approving Axa's controlling stake in National Mutual was that ownership of the parent's Asian businesses be transferred to the subsidiary.
Axa-UAP applied for to a licence to sell life insurance in Shanghai just this year, despite National Mutual having worked for years to secure a licence in the same market.
News of the success of Axa-UAP's application came during a visit to China this month by French President Jacques Chirac.
Tomlinson flew to Paris last week to discuss the China licence and other issues with Axa-UAP management.
Under a cooperation agreement between National Mutual and Axa-UAP, the parent agreed that its Asian businesses will be managed "and, if agreed, ultimately owned" by National Mutual.
The agreement also says Axa will transfer its Asian life insurance businesses to the National Mutual group over the six years from June 1995.
But Axa-UAP has rejected calls by the FIRB for it to hand ownership of the China business to National Mutual.
It has said it appears "probable" it will work with National Mutual in China but it did not yet know under what terms.
Both parties are waiting to know the terms of the licence.
